issues.legal_issue: Conduct predating a statutory eviction provision may be considered when determining whether a tenant failed to pay rent regularly without sufficient cause.
material_facts: The tenant’s repeated non-payment began before the relevant eviction procedure was enacted and continued afterward.
The landlord sought eviction on the ground of failure to pay rent regularly without sufficient cause.
issues.conclusion: The decision-maker could consider the tenant’s pre-enactment conduct in deciding whether the statutory ground for eviction was established; doing so did not apply the statute retrospectively.
issues.legal_principle: A statute is not applied retrospectively merely because part of the facts or requisites relevant to its operation arose before it was enacted. The Court applied section 9(1)(ii) of the Punjab Security of Land Tenures Act, 1953, through the eviction procedure in section 14-A(1). No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.tenant_eviction_proceeding: A landlord pursued a proceeding to evict a tenant.
predicates.eviction_sought_for_irregular_nonpayment: The landlord sought eviction because the tenant allegedly failed to pay rent regularly without sufficient cause.
predicates.relevant_rent_conduct_predated_enactment: The tenant’s rent-related conduct relevant to the eviction claim began before the governing eviction procedure was enacted.
predicates.pre_enactment_conduct_may_be_considered: Conduct occurring before enactment may be considered in deciding whether the eviction ground is established.

issues.definition: When a landlord seeks eviction for irregular non-payment, relevant rent conduct that began before enactment may be considered.

issues.legal_issue: Timely payment of arrears in a rent-recovery proceeding does not prevent eviction on the separate ground of irregular non-payment without sufficient cause.
material_facts: The tenant paid the arrears within the time fixed in the rent-recovery proceeding.
The landlord had also pursued a separate eviction proceeding based on the tenant’s alleged failure to pay rent regularly without sufficient cause.
The tenant’s rent-payment conduct supported the separate eviction ground.
issues.conclusion: Although the tenant could not be evicted under the arrears-recovery provision after paying within the time allowed, eviction could still be ordered under the separate provision for an established ground of eviction.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 14-A(1) and 14-A(ii) serve different purposes: section 14-A(ii) provides for eviction following non-compliance with an order to deposit arrears, while section 14-A(1), read with section 9(1), provides for eviction on the grounds specified in the Act, including irregular payment without sufficient cause. The provisions are not inconsistent. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.tenant_eviction_proceeding: A landlord pursued a proceeding to evict a tenant.
predicates.arrears_paid_within_allowed_time: The tenant paid the arrears within the time allowed in a separate rent-recovery proceeding.
predicates.separate_irregular_nonpayment_ground_est: The tenant’s failure to pay rent regularly without sufficient cause was established as an independent ground for eviction.
predicates.timely_arrears_payment_does_not_bar_inde: Payment of arrears within the allowed time does not prevent eviction on a separately established ground.

issues.definition: If a tenant pays arrears on time but an independent ground of irregular non-payment is established, the timely payment does not prevent eviction on that ground.

issues.legal_issue: Repeated non-payment of rent was not supported by sufficient cause where the tenant relied on disputes about the leased property and rent calculation but did not use the available means to address an alleged refusal to accept rent.
material_facts: The tenant did not pay rent for successive years, and the landlord had to obtain recovery through court proceedings.
The tenant attributed non-payment to a defective water supply and uncertainty about the rent payable under the statutory rent limit.
The tenant alleged that the landlord had refused payment but did not notify the appropriate authority or seek the available protection for a landlord’s refusal to accept rent.
The Court found that the tenant had used the disputes as pretexts to avoid payment.
issues.conclusion: The tenant failed to establish sufficient cause for the repeated irregular non-payment, and the eviction ground was made out.
issues.legal_principle: Section 9(1)(ii) permits eviction for failure to pay rent regularly without sufficient cause. Section 14-A(1) provides the eviction procedure, while section 14-A(iii) supplies a means for a tenant to report a landlord’s refusal to accept rent or other specified rent-related conduct. The Court also considered the statutory rent limit in section 12. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: tenant_eviction_proceeding and repeated_rent_nonpayment and tenant_asserted_payment_obstacle and tenant_did_not_use_available_refusal_remedy

predicates.tenant_eviction_proceeding: A landlord pursued a proceeding to evict a tenant.
predicates.repeated_rent_nonpayment: The tenant failed to pay rent over successive rental periods, requiring the landlord to seek recovery through court proceedings.
predicates.tenant_asserted_payment_obstacle: The tenant relied on a dispute about the leased property or uncertainty about the rent payable as a reason for non-payment.
predicates.tenant_did_not_use_available_refusal_rem: Despite alleging that the landlord refused rent, the tenant did not report the refusal to the appropriate authority or seek the available protection.
predicates.sufficient_cause_for_irregular_nonpaymen: The tenant’s reasons did not sufficiently explain the repeated failure to pay rent regularly.

issues.definition: When repeated non-payment is accompanied by asserted payment obstacles but the tenant does not use the available means to address an alleged refusal to accept rent, sufficient cause for the irregular non-payment is not established.
